verdict: Uber grew revenue 15% to $9.9B on 2.6 billion trips, swung to a $652M operating profit, and posted $1.4B of profit for shareholders — flattered by about $1B of paper gains on its investment stakes.

segments.name: Mobility
segments.note: Rides — revenue jumped 34%, even after business-model changes in some countries moved $207M of selling costs into contra revenue (counted against revenue).

segments.name: Delivery
segments.note: Uber Eats food and grocery delivery — growth was held back 11 points by business-model changes that moved $322M of costs into contra revenue.

segments.name: Freight
segments.note: Trucking brokerage — revenue per load and volumes both fell in a weak freight market.

opex.name: Operations and support
opex.note: Support for riders, drivers, restaurants and shippers.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Advertising and promotions to win riders, drivers and merchants.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the app, matching and pricing technology.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — finance, legal and the back office.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Wear and tear on servers, offices and equipment.

otherDetail: Other income, net of $1,331M — including a $1,000M net unrealized gain from revaluing Uber's equity investments and a $204M gain on selling part of the Careem business — plus $5M of income from equity method investments, less $155M of interest expense.
follow100Note: Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Net income of $1,700M is the total including non-controlling interests; $271M belongs to those partners, leaving $1,429M attributable to Uber shareholders (the $0.66 EPS figure).

takeaways.title: The core business swung to profit
takeaways.text: Income from operations was $652M, up $794M from a $142M loss a year ago, and Adjusted EBITDA nearly doubled to $1,283M as Mobility and Delivery growth outpaced costs.

takeaways.title: Bookings kept growing
takeaways.text: Gross Bookings rose 22% to $37.6B on 2.6 billion trips (+24%). Mobility revenue jumped 34% to $5,537M and Delivery rose 6% to $3,119M; Freight fell 17% to $1,280M in a soft trucking market.

takeaways.title: Paper gains padded the bottom line
takeaways.text: About $1.0B of the profit was a net unrealized gain on Uber's stakes in other companies — Aurora up $659M and Didi up $414M, partly offset by a $91M drop in Grab — plus a $204M gain on the Careem sale. Free cash flow was $768M.

oneTimers: Other income includes a $1,000M net unrealized gain (pre-tax) from revaluing Uber's equity investments — a paper gain that could reverse if those stocks fall — and a $204M gain on the sale of Uber's interest in the Careem non-ridesharing business.
